Hi Ella 

Thanks for taking the time today  great conversation with the Infra and product teams. Quick recap and proposed next steps so we can size the right configuration and cost estimate:

Recap / SLOs you shared
- 95th percentile latency target: <= 200ms for text-generation API (prompt+response p95)
- Expected steady-state throughput: ~120 requests/sec (concurrent stream and non-stream mix)
- Peak concurrency expected: ~40 concurrent user sessions
- Streaming: yes, many flows require token-by-token streaming for progressive UI (approx 60% of calls)
- Average request size: ~180 tokens input, ~120 tokens output

Requested from our side
- Please confirm whether p99 matters separately (you mentioned p99 < 800ms may be ok)
- Confirm ratio of streaming vs non-streaming calls during peak (you said ~60/40)
- If you can, fill the attached SLO_questionnaire.xlsx with current traffic patterns and any retention/audit needs (we use this for accurate capacity modeling)

Cost / performance levers we'll evaluate (we discussed these on the call):
- Continuous batching: merges concurrent small requests into sub-batches to improve throughput at low latency impact
- KV/prefix caching: for repeat prompts (e.g., system messages, reused contexts) to reduce repeated compute
- Quantization profiles: exploring int8 / q4/ q5 families to reduce GPU memory and speed up inference for non-critical flows
- Model variants: suggest a lower-latency 13B variant for interactive flows and a higher-quality 34B for background bulk jobs

Next steps / owners
- Ella / Infra: confirm streaming ratio + populate questionnaire (action: Ella; timeline: EOD Wed 10/14)
- Redwood (Neha & Rishi): run modeling pass and share latency/throughput tradeoffs by Fri 10/16
- Marcus / Marissa: produce draft pricing for both reserved and burst scenarios and include estimate for Dedicated vs Hosted

Attachment: SLO_questionnaire.xlsx (please attach traffic patterns if possible)

If anything above is incorrect, call it out and I'll update. Thanks again  we'll aim to get the modeling back on Friday.

Hi all 

Thanks  ran a quick modeling pass based on the initial traffic sample in the drive and the call notes. High-level findings and recommended configuration to hit p95 ~200ms at ~120 req/s (mixed streaming):

Summary estimates
- With continuous batching + 10% KV cache hit: p95 ~ 180-220ms depending on model variant and GPU family (A100 vs RTX-class)
- Streaming tightness: keep per-token scheduling latency <10ms; batching windows <=8ms for the streaming queue to avoid noticeable UI lag
- Throughput: a single A100 (40GB) with optimized kernels can handle ~80-90 concurrent short requests for a 13B quantized int8 profile; you'd need 2 nodes for comfortable headroom for 120 req/s bursty traffic

Recommended levers (priority order)
1) Continuous batching: enable adaptive batching with a max window of 8ms for streaming and 20ms for non-streaming flows. This recovers GPU efficiency without violating interactive latency SLOs.
2) Prefix/KV caching: target 10-25% hit rate for common system prompts this reduces peak compute by similar fraction. Cache TTLs of 5-15 mins are typical for conversational widgets.
3) Quantization profile: recommend q4_0 or int8 (AMP) for interactive 13B variant  tradeoff: small quality delta vs 2-3x throughput improvement. Produce sample outputs to validate quality regression with Orchid product team.
4) Model routing: serve 13B q4_0 for interactive flows; fall back to 34B full-precision for long-form generation or QA pipelines where quality trumps latency.
5) Autoscaling + reserved capacity: propose Dedicated pool with 2x A100 nodes for steady 120 req/s with burst capacity to 4 nodes for 300 req/s peaks. Consider pre-provisioning GPU headroom for failover.

Cost notes (ballpark, to be refined after full questionnaire)
- Hosted (on-demand): ~ $5k-$8k/day for sustained 120 req/s on premium GPUs (depends on region & instance type)
- Dedicated (committed): monthly reserved capacity with 2x A100 equivalent could reduce unit cost by ~35-45% vs on-demand

Actionables / next steps
- Redwood (Rishi + Neha): final modeling pass after full hour-of-peak CSV, and example quality checks for q4_0 outputs (action: Rishi; timeline: 48 hours after questionnaire)
- Orchid (Ella): confirm any regulatory/PHI constraints that affect model selection and KMS (action: Ella; timeline: EOD Wed 10/14)
- Contract/Commercial: Marcus/Marissa to prepare a preliminary cost model and reserved pricing once we finalize node counts (action: Marcus; timeline: next Tue 10/20)

Attachments: redwood_latency_modeling.pdf (adds more detail on kernel selection and latency curves).

Let me know if you want a quick hangout to walk through numbers.
